newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM Howard hit by expenses scandal.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard hit by expenses scandal.

text.p: Australia's conservative government was under fire on Thursday for keeping under wraps an investigation into a senator accused of fiddling his expenses.

The Labor opposition demanded that Prime Minister John Howard explain his response to a police investigation into senator Bob Woods, who has also attracted media attention after an ex-lover's accusations that he had harrassed her.
Labor said the expenses investigation and Howard's handling of it was example of the sleazy pattern of behavior in that had characterised the government since it was elected in March 1996.
Two other junior members of the government resigned late last year over conflicts of interest in their business dealings.
"It is symptomatic of what has become a very messy way of dealing with the issues of standards of conduct of ministers and members of the executive," opposition leader Kim Beazley said.
Politicians' personal lives are not a political concern in Australia and Labor has focussed on the expenses probe and Howard's handling of it, not Woods' extra-marital affair.
Woods, who held the junior position of parliamentary health secretary, announced he was quitting politics on Monday to spend more time with his family.
The police investigation was revealed the next day.
Since announcing his resignation the married senator and his former lover Roxanne Cameron, a Liberal party adviser, have also traded accusations of harrassment and threats of legal action.
Woods' office has confirmed that the police are investigating but the senator, who denies the allegations.

Labor has accused Howard -- who during the election campaing had pledged to clean up government -- of breaking his own code of conduct and misleading the public over when he learned of the police investigation.
Howard said on Wednesday that Woods told him of the investigation only 10 days before.
But he told Parliament on Thursday he had forgotten that Attorney-General Daryl Williams told him of the probe late last year.
"I have nothing to hide, nothing to be ashamed of," Howard told parliament on Thursday.
Deputy opposition leader Gareth Evans on Wednesday accused Howard of running a sleazy government, saying there was "a sleaze factor manifestly at work" in the administration.
